correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<r<1/2, simultaneous equality of closed neighborhoods of two adjacent sorted points is equivalent to vacancy of the two translated boundary arcs of length equal to their gap. Uniform positive symmetric-difference measure excludes nonlocal twins with probability tending to 1; between endpoints of a true-twin interval the boundary-arc inclusions enforce contiguous equivalence classes. At finitely many consecutive gaps, Exp(1) scaled spacings and two independent rate-one Poisson boundary processes yield iid Bernoulli good marks of probability E exp(-2L)=1/3. Two far-apart roots give covariance o(1) of any bounded local run pattern; bad-good^(j-1)-bad gives C_(n,j)/n->(4/9)3^(-(j-1)) jointly for finitely many j, and bad-gap frequency yields Q_n/n->2/3. Normalizing by Q_n gives geometric class size with parameter 2/3. Pair-count concentration T_n/n->1/2 follows by truncating nonnegative sum binom(j,2)C_(n,j) and citing the existing expected pair count E T_n/n->1/2; the truncation tail is controlled in expectation, not guessed from fixed-j limits. Scope fixed radius and iid circle model. Independently tested direct closed-neighborhood grouping on random graphs at radii 0.10,0.30,0.47 and n=55,110 (120 replicates each), agreeing with first five run-frequency predictions and pair density; these tests are finite evidence, not the limiting proof.

value.rationale: The random circle graph has a first-order definable equivalence relation (equality of closed neighborhoods); the asymptotic size distribution of its equivalence classes and proportion surviving quotient are intrinsic graph invariants relevant to first-order model theory, random geometric graphs and compression. A full universal geometric spectrum with quantified LLN is beyond the prior expected pair count and independent of radius. This is substantive structural information, not a reparameterized first moment.
